program_or_activity: Risk Management Agency Federal Crop Insurance Corporation

q4_2025_scorecard.recovery_process: AIPs are notified through CARS; reported overpayments are then tracked, collected, and verified through RMA accounting systems.

rma_fy2024_review.selection_factor_published: Approved Insurance Provider servicing the policy

period_reconciliation.sra_definition: A reinsurance year begins July 1, ends June 30 of the following year, and is identified by the year containing June.

closed_internal_only.basis: COM-23-001 identifies the FY2024 review as reinsurance year 2022; the SRA definition converts that label to July 2021 through June 2022, matching both PaymentAccuracy sources.
The FY2024 annual row completely separates overpayments, underpayments, technically improper payments, and unknown payments and reconciles those categories to the improper-payment total.

open.remaining_need: sample frame, strata, weights, projection details, and variance method
included and excluded payment and policy categories
estimator, weights, variance, and sampled-error-to-dollar projection
excluded policy or payment categories and rationale
complete classification rules and separation from collectible or recoverable overpayments
amount-level lineage from estimated errors to established debt, collections, prevention, and control cost

evidence_boundaries: The FY2024 values are statistical estimates for a sampled payment universe, not a transaction-level list of identified debts.
Improper payments and outside-agency-control root causes are not findings of fraud, waste, or abuse.
The scorecard recovery-process description does not identify how much of the FY2024 estimate was collectible, collected, or prevented.
The rounded 467 million and 107 million root-cause categories are not savings estimates and cannot be reconciled below their displayed precision.
The margin of error applies to the published estimate and does not establish recoverability or net fiscal benefit.
No savings score is allowed without debt lineage, appeal and reversal treatment, collections, prevention attribution, and control cost.
